# Student Body for your studio

**A guide to setting up and running your studio.**

Edition October 2026 · Describes Student Body as of 6 November 2026

---

## How to read this guide

This guide covers everything from setting up your studio on Student Body to managing classes,
bookings, and your day-to-day schedule.

You don't need to read it all at once. Start with Part 1 to get everything set up, then come back to
individual chapters whenever you need them.

At the end, you'll find two short guides to share with your team: one for your front desk staff and
one for your instructors.

The screens in this guide come from Estúdio Âmbar, a made-up studio with made-up students, so the
names and numbers you see are examples.

### Who each chapter is for

Each chapter shows who it is for, beside its title:

| Tag | Who |
|---|---|
| Owner | The person who owns and manages the studio's Student Body account |
| Manager | A team member with the Manager role |
| Staff | Someone with the Staff role, usually working at the front desk |
| Instructor | An instructor listed on your studio's roster |

### A few things to look out for

> **Heads up**
>
> Important things to know before making a change.

> **Good to know**
>
> Extra information that might come in handy.

### One last thing

When we put something in quotes, like "Launch readiness," that's the exact wording you'll see on
Student Body.

Student Body is always evolving, so some screens might look a little different from what's shown
here. This guide reflects the platform as of 6 November 2026. If something doesn't match, follow
what's on screen or email us at support@studentbody.pt.

## Welcome

Student Body helps students discover movement classes they'll love, while giving studios and
instructors more ways to connect with students.

Students can explore classes, get to know the instructors behind them, and find experiences that
suit their interests, schedules, and preferences. They can also follow their favorite instructors
and studios to keep up with what's happening.

A few things worth knowing about how Student Body works:

- **Your students stay yours**\
  Your relationships with your students belong to you. We're here to help you build on them, not
  get in the way.
- **You keep your booking system**\
  You don't need to change how you manage bookings. Students can discover your classes on Student
  Body and book through the system you already use.
- **Payments go directly to you**\
  If you choose to accept bookings through Student Body, payments go directly to your own Stripe
  account. You remain the seller, and Student Body never holds your money. We'll cover this in more
  detail in Part 5.
- **Your studio, your data**\
  You can download your studio's data or close your Student Body account whenever you choose.

# Part 1 — Before you start

What Student Body can do for your studio, what it costs, what you'll need, and what to expect as you
get set up.

## 1. How Student Body works with your studio [Owner]

If you already use a booking system, you can keep using it just as you do today.
Your students won't need to change how they book classes.

What Student Body adds:

- **A studio page** where students can discover your studio, explore your classes, meet your
  instructors, and learn more about your space.
- **Detailed class pages** that explain what to expect, who each class is for, and what the
  experience feels like.
- **More ways to get discovered** by students looking for classes that fit their interests,
  schedules, and preferences.
- **A studio dashboard** where you and your team can manage your information and keep everything up
  to date.

### How a student books

Student Body supports a few ways to book a class:

| Booking method | What the student sees | Where the booking goes |
|---|---|---|
| Your existing booking system | "Book on [studio name]" | Your booking system, just like booking through your website |
| WhatsApp | "Book on WhatsApp" and the class price | To your studio's WhatsApp number, as a request already written. Students pay you directly |
| Contact the studio | Your contact details | Directly to your studio |
| Book on Student Body | "Reserve" and the class price | Through Student Body, with payment sent directly to your Stripe account |

You can choose how bookings work for each class and change this later.

If you'd like to accept bookings directly on Student Body, Part 5 explains how that works.

### Keeping your schedule up to date

If your schedule is in Acuity, bsport, or YOGO, you can connect it to Student Body, and it will sync
automatically every hour. When you add or reschedule a class there, those changes will appear on
Student Body without any extra work from you. If you don't use one of these systems, you can
schedule your classes directly on Student Body (chapter 13).

Chapter 11 explains which information syncs automatically and what you'll need to update yourself.

## 2. What Student Body costs [Owner]

You'll find our current pricing on our pricing page at https://www.studentbody.pt/en/pricing.

If you have a question about what your studio would pay, email us at support@studentbody.pt.

## 3. What you'll need [Owner]

Having these ready will make setting up your studio quicker. You can add or change any of them
later.

### About your studio

- The email address you'll use to sign in to Student Body.
- Your logo and photos of your studio and classes. Portrait images (2:3) work best.
- A short description of the studio, in your own words.
- Your website and Instagram account.

### Your locations

- Your studio's address, including any important arrival details like door codes, buzzers, or floor
  numbers.
- Anything students should know before arriving, such as parking, changing rooms, or what to bring.

### Your instructors

- Your instructors' names and email addresses, so they can create their own profiles.
- A photo and short bio for each instructor.
- Who you'd like to help manage your studio on Student Body, and which roles they should have
  (chapter 10).

### Your classes

- If your schedule is in Acuity, bsport, or YOGO, your login or booking page details, so you can
  connect it (chapter 11).
- Your current class prices.
- Your cancellation policy.

## 4. Getting started, step by step [Owner]

Here's how to get your studio set up and ready for students to discover, in seven simple steps.

| | Who | What happens | What students can see |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | You | Select "Request access" on studentbody.pt/studios and tell us about your studio | Nothing yet |
| 2 | Student Body | We'll email you an invitation to create your studio | Nothing yet |
| 3 | You | You follow the link in the invitation, sign in, and create your studio in a few short steps | Nothing yet |
| 4 | You | You connect your booking system, or add your classes and schedule directly on Student Body | Nothing yet |
| 5 | You | You publish your classes and request to go live | Your studio page, if someone has the direct link. Classes aren't visible yet |
| 6 | Student Body | We'll review your studio, usually within one day, and approve it to go live | Your studio page, classes, and listing in Discover |
| 7 | You | Share your studio page on your website, Instagram, or anywhere else your students can find you | Everything |

> **Good to know**
>
> Until step 6, your studio is still in draft mode. You can preview your own page while setting
> things up, but students won't be able to discover it on Student Body.

# Part 2 — Setting up

How to access your studio dashboard, review your information, and set up your studio profile,
locations, team, classes, and schedule.

## 5. Accessing your studio dashboard [Owner · Manager · Staff]

### Creating your studio

Studios join Student Body by invitation. To join, select "Request access" on studentbody.pt/studios
and tell us about your studio. We'll email you an invitation with a link to create your studio.

Follow the link and sign in. You'll be taken to a page called "Create your studio," which walks you
through a few short steps:

- **Basics:** Your studio's name and handle. Your handle becomes the web address of your studio
  page. The invite code from your invitation is filled in for you.
- **Disciplines:** The types of movement your studio offers.
- **Location:** Your studio's address. You can skip this and add your locations later (chapter 9).
- **Details:** A short description of your studio, your website and Instagram, and a public contact
  email.
- **Team:** Invite instructors who are already on Student Body, using their handle. You can also do
  this later (chapter 10).
- **Import:** Connect Acuity, bsport, or YOGO, or paste your schedule as a spreadsheet (CSV). If you
  don't use a booking system, skip this step and add your classes yourself (chapter 11).
- **Review:** Choose whether your studio should go live or stay a draft for now.

Selecting "Create studio" in the first step creates your studio as a draft. When you've finished
the last step, you'll be taken to your studio dashboard.

> **Heads up**
>
> "Keep as draft" is already selected in the review step, so the last button reads "Finish" and your
> studio stays a draft. We won't review it until you select "Make studio public" on your Home page,
> which you can do whenever your classes are ready (chapter 14). If they're ready now, choose "Go
> live" instead. The last button will then read "Go live," and selecting it sends your studio to us
> for review straight away.

**Signing in.** You don't need a password to use Student Body. You can sign in using a link sent to
your email, or with Google or Apple. Make sure to use the same email address that received your
invitation, because the invite code only works for that address. If you need to use a different
email, contact us for a new invitation.

> **Good to know**
>
> If you're new to Student Body, you'll also be asked to accept the Terms of Service and confirm
> that you're at least 16 years old.

### Finding your dashboard later

Go to app.studentbody.pt and sign in. If you own the studio, you'll land on your studio's Home page.
Everyone else on your team can select their profile picture in the top-right corner, then select
"Studio Dashboard."

### The dashboard at a glance

The menu on the left is divided into four sections:

| Group | Pages | What they're for |
|---|---|---|
| **Studio** | Home, Schedule, Bookings, Classes, Locations, Share, View profile | Everything you need to manage your studio day to day |
| **Insights** | Overview, Audience, Reports, Feedback | Information about your classes, students, and studio performance |
| **Team** | Team members, Activity | Your instructors, team members, and recent activity |
| **Settings** | Studio profile, Connected apps, Packs, Discounts, Payments, Plan & billing | Your studio settings, connected services, and payment options |

"View profile" opens your public studio page, which is what students see. To make changes to your
studio's information, go to "Studio profile" under Settings.

The bar at the top of your dashboard shows your studio's name, number of instructors, upcoming
sessions, followers, and current status: Draft, Under review, or Live (chapter 14).

### Getting to know your dashboard

The first time you open Home, you'll get a short tour of the dashboard and its features. You can
take the tour again anytime by going to your Account page and selecting "Replay studio dashboard
tour." You'll also find a small "?" on each card on the Home page. Select it for more information
about what that card shows.

### Who can access your dashboard

What you can see and manage depends on your role. Managers have access to every page except
Payments and Plan & billing, and only the owner can download the full data export or close the
studio. Staff can access Home and Schedule.

You can find the full breakdown of permissions in Appendix B.

## 6. Reviewing your studio setup [Owner · Manager]

Before going live, take a few minutes to review everything and make sure it's accurate.

Here's what to check:

1. **Your public studio page:** Select "View profile" in the menu to see what students will see. Check
   your studio description, photos, instructors, and address.
2. **`Settings → Studio profile`:** Review your studio's information and make any changes you'd like
   (chapter 8).
3. **Your locations:** Check that your studio's address and arrival instructions are correct
   (chapter 9).
4. **`Team → Team members`:** Review your instructors, including their photos and bios (chapter
   10).
5. **Classes:** Check your classes, including their names, descriptions, and the details that help
   students decide which classes are right for them (chapter 12).
6. **Schedule:** Make sure your classes appear on the correct days and times (chapter 13).

Your studio won't be publicly discoverable until you've requested to go live and we've approved it.

## 7. The studio agreement [Owner]

The studio agreement will be the contract between your studio and Student Body. We're preparing
it with our lawyers, so there's nothing to accept yet.

Once it's published, you'll find it under `Settings → Plan & billing`, in the "Studio agreement" section.
Only the studio owner will be able to accept it.

## 8. Your studio profile [Owner · Manager]

Your public studio page is where students can get to know your studio, explore your classes, and
find your instructors. You can manage everything that appears on this page under
`Settings → Studio profile`.

| Section | What you can manage | Where students see it |
|---|---|---|
| **Basics** | Studio logo, name, and profile URL | Your logo and name appear on your studio page, along with its web address |
| **About** | Studio description and a short announcement (up to 300 characters) | Your description appears near the top of your page, with the announcement displayed underneath in italics |
| **Photos & videos** | Your gallery, including the order of your images and videos | Your media gallery appears at the top of your studio page, with the first item used as the cover |
| **Disciplines** | The types of movement your studio offers | Displayed as labels beneath your studio description |
| **Contact & Links** | Your website, Instagram, and public contact email | In the "Connect" section of your studio page |
| Timezone | Your studio's local timezone | Used to display class times correctly |
| Default free-cancellation window | How far in advance students can cancel without a penalty | Applies only to classes booked directly through Student Body (Part 5) |
| Content language | The language you use for your studio's information | Students viewing Student Body in another language can read translated content |
| **Student communications** | Booking confirmation emails and other booking notifications | Applies only to bookings made directly through Student Body (Part 5) |
| **Theme** | Your studio's accent color | Used on your public studio page and dashboard |
| **Visibility** | Whether your studio is Public or Draft | Controls your studio's visibility (chapter 14) |

When you're finished updating your studio profile, select "Save changes" in the bar at the bottom of your screen.

> **Heads up**
>
> "Save changes" appears in a bar at the bottom of your screen once you've changed something. Most
> changes won't be saved until you select it, although some settings under Student communications
> save automatically.

> **Heads up**
>
> Changing your "Profile URL" will change the link to your studio page. Any links you've previously
> shared using the old address will stop working.

### A few tips for your studio profile

**Your studio description**\
Think about what makes your studio special. What's the space like? Who are your classes for? What
can students expect when they visit?

Keep it natural and easy to read, with short paragraphs. If you offer classes in more than one
language, it's worth mentioning that too.

Students can translate your page, but it'll read best in the language you've selected under
"Content language."

**Your photos**\
Use real photos of your studio, instructors, and classes to give students a feel for your space.
Portrait photos work best in the gallery, and we'd recommend avoiding stock images.

## 9. Your locations [Owner · Manager]

Your locations are the places where your classes take place. Students can see the address, map, and
arrival instructions on your studio page and individual class pages.

Go to "Locations" in your studio dashboard and select "Add location."

Here's what you'll need to complete:

- **Name, Address, and City:** These fields are required for every location.
- **Address:** Start typing and select the correct address from the suggestions. This automatically
  places your location on the map.
- **Unit / floor:** Add a room name, floor number, or other details to help students find the right
  space.
- **Arrival details:** Use "Getting here," "Parking," "How to get in," "Amenities," and
  "Accessibility" to add one detail per line. "How to get in" is especially helpful for new
  students, so include details like door codes, buzzers, or floor numbers.
- **Show the exact location publicly:** When this is on, students can see your full address and a
  map pin. When it's off, they'll see the general area until they book.
- **Off-site event location:** Use this for a space you borrow for an occasional event. It won't
  appear on your studio page.
- **Timezone:** Leave this set to "Inherit the studio's timezone" unless your location is in a
  different timezone.

> **Heads up**
>
> Always add new locations through "Locations" in your studio dashboard. Locations created within
> the class editor belong to the person who created them, not the studio.

> **Good to know**
>
> A location will appear on your public studio page once you have a published class scheduled
> there.

If you have more than one location, set each class's default location in the class editor
(chapter 12). Students will see which location each class takes place at.

## 10. Your team [Owner · Manager]

Go to `Team → Team members` to see the instructors associated with your studio. Each instructor
appears on your public studio page and on the classes they teach.

### Adding instructors who aren't on Student Body yet

You can add instructors to your studio's roster even if they don't have a Student Body account.
Under "Add people," select "Add someone not on the platform." Enter their name and
disciplines, upload a photo, and confirm that they've agreed to be listed. They'll appear on your
roster as a placeholder, marked "Unclaimed."

- **Edit details:** You can update a placeholder's photo, disciplines, and bio. Their name can't be
  changed here.
- **Claim link:** Sends an instructor a link to their email address so they can claim their
  placeholder profile. Their classes and teaching history will be linked to their new profile. Each
  link can only be used once and expires after 30 days.

### Inviting instructors already on Student Body

If an instructor already has a Student Body profile, you can invite them to join your studio's
roster. Under "Add people," search for their name or handle and select "Send invite."
They'll receive a notification and an email inviting them to join your studio. Once they accept,
they'll appear on your roster. You can also select "Generate invite link" to share a link directly.
Each link can only be used once and expires after 30 days.

### Adding someone who doesn't teach

A manager or someone at the front desk who doesn't teach can use your studio dashboard too. Under
"Add people," select "Add someone who doesn't teach." Enter their email address, choose Manager or
Staff, and select "Send invite." They'll receive an email, and once they accept, they can use your
dashboard in that role. They don't need an instructor profile, and they don't appear on your public
studio page or as the instructor of a class. Only that email address can accept the invite, and it
expires after 30 days.

If you've already added an instructor as a placeholder and they have an existing Student Body
profile, you may see "Possible match: [name]" on your roster. Select "Link profile" to connect the
two.

### Managing team roles and permissions

To change someone's permissions, open their profile on your roster and select "Role & access."

| Role | Can |
|---|---|
| **Manager** | Run the studio: its profile, team, locations, connected apps, classes, schedule, packs and discounts, and view bookings, insights, and feedback. Not payments or plan and billing |
| **Staff** | Manage the schedule and check-ins |
| **Member** | No access to the studio dashboard. This is the default role for instructors until you change it |

> **Heads up**
>
> Changes to roles and selecting "Remove" take effect immediately, without a confirmation step.

> **Good to know**
>
> On your roster, someone who joined with "Add someone who doesn't teach" shows "Doesn't teach," and
> the instructor settings below don't apply to them.

There are three additional settings for instructors who also manage their own classes:

- **Can schedule at our locations:** Allows the instructor to schedule their own classes at your
  studio's locations.
- **Can take payment for their own classes here:** Allows the instructor to accept payments for
  their own classes at your studio.
- **Can edit class details:** Allows the instructor to make changes to their own class information.

These settings only apply to instructors who publish and manage their own classes at your studio's
locations. If that doesn't apply to your team, you can leave them turned off.

## 11. Connecting your schedule [Owner · Manager]

If your schedule is in Acuity, bsport, or YOGO, you can connect it under `Settings → Connected apps`,
and Student Body will keep it in sync every hour. Find your booking system below. If you don't use
one of these, see "Adding your schedule yourself" at the end of this chapter.

### Connecting Acuity

If your schedule is in Acuity, you can connect it and continue managing your classes there as usual.

1. Go to `Settings → Connected apps` and select "Connect Acuity." You'll be taken to Acuity to sign
   in and allow Student Body to access your schedule. Once connected, Acuity will send you back to
   Student Body.
2. Select "Sync & review." Student Body will import your classes, upcoming sessions, instructors,
   and locations. You'll also see which instructors have been matched to existing profiles and
   which are new.
3. Under "Not on the schedule," you'll find classes that don't have any upcoming sessions. Select
   any you'd like to import as drafts.
4. Check the box confirming that the instructors listed teach for your studio or have given
   permission to be included. New instructors will be added as placeholders.
5. Select "Confirm import" to finish.

Everything will be imported as a draft. You'll need to publish your classes (chapter 12) and make
your studio live (chapter 14) before students can discover them.

Bookings will continue through Acuity, with each session linking directly to the corresponding
booking page.

### What syncs automatically

With "Keep my schedule in sync automatically" turned on, Student Body checks your Acuity schedule
every hour. Here's what updates automatically:

- **New sessions:** Upcoming sessions for published classes will appear automatically.
- **Schedule changes:** Sessions moved or cancelled in Acuity will also be updated on Student Body.
- **Availability:** The number of available spots is refreshed.
- **New classes:** New class types added in Acuity will appear as drafts for you to review and
  publish.

### What doesn't change

Some information stays exactly as you've set it up on Student Body, even when your Acuity schedule
syncs.

- **Your edits:** Class names, descriptions, and other details you've updated on Student Body won't
  be overwritten by Acuity.
- **New instructors:** Classes from newly added instructors won't appear automatically. Select
  "Sync & review" again to import them.

> **Heads up**
>
> Make all schedule changes, including cancellations, directly in Acuity. If you cancel a session
> only on Student Body, it will reappear during the next hourly sync.

> **Good to know**
>
> "Refresh from Acuity" brings in the class names, descriptions, images, and booking links Acuity has
> now. Classes you've edited on Student Body keep your names, descriptions, and images: only their
> booking links are updated.

To stop syncing your schedule, select "Disconnect." Your existing classes and sessions will
stay on Student Body, but they'll no longer update automatically. To completely remove Student
Body's access to your Acuity account, you'll also need to remove Student Body from your connected
apps in Acuity.

### Connecting bsport

If your schedule is in bsport, you can connect it and continue managing your classes there as usual.

1. Go to `Settings → Connected apps` and choose BSport. Paste the link to the page on your website where your bsport booking calendar is embedded, the page your
   students use to book. You can also enter your bsport company ID instead.
2. Select "Sync & review." Student Body will show the classes, upcoming sessions, instructors, and
   locations it found, and which instructors have been matched to existing profiles.
3. Under "Not on the schedule," select any classes without upcoming sessions that you'd like to
   import as drafts.
4. Check the box confirming that the instructors listed teach for your studio or have given
   permission to be included. New instructors will be added as placeholders.
5. Select "Confirm import" to finish.

Your classes will be imported as drafts, unless you check "Publish imported classes immediately."
Bookings will continue through bsport, with each session linking directly to its booking page.

With "Keep my schedule in sync automatically" turned on, Student Body checks your bsport schedule
every hour. New sessions for published classes appear automatically, and new classes arrive as
drafts for you to review. Classes from newly added instructors won't appear until you select "Sync &
review" again.

> **Heads up**
>
> Make all schedule changes, including cancellations, directly in bsport.

> **Good to know**
>
> "Refresh descriptions & images" brings in the class names, descriptions, and images bsport has now.
> Classes you've edited on Student Body keep your names, descriptions, and images.

To stop syncing your schedule, select "Disconnect." Your existing classes and sessions will stay on
Student Body.

### Connecting YOGO

If your schedule is in YOGO, you can connect it and continue managing your classes there as usual.

1. Go to `Settings → Connected apps` and choose YOGO. Paste the link to your YOGO booking page, or to the page on your website where your YOGO calendar is embedded.
2. Select "Sync & review." Student Body will show the classes, upcoming sessions, instructors, and
   locations it found, and which instructors have been matched to existing profiles.
3. Under "Not on the schedule," select any classes without upcoming sessions that you'd like to
   import as drafts.
4. Check the box confirming that the instructors listed teach for your studio or have given
   permission to be included. New instructors will be added as placeholders.
5. Select "Confirm import" to finish.

Your classes will be imported as drafts, unless you check "Publish imported classes immediately."
Bookings will continue through YOGO, with each session linking directly to its booking page.

With "Keep my schedule in sync automatically" turned on, Student Body checks your YOGO schedule every
hour. New sessions for published classes appear automatically, and new classes arrive as drafts for
you to review. Classes from newly added instructors won't appear until you select "Sync & review"
again.

> **Heads up**
>
> Make all schedule changes, including cancellations, directly in YOGO.

To stop syncing your schedule, select "Disconnect." Your existing classes and sessions will stay on
Student Body.

### Adding your schedule yourself

If you don't use Acuity, bsport, or YOGO, you can still bring your schedule to Student Body in one of
two ways:

- **Paste your schedule:** Go to `Settings → Connected apps`, choose "Manual import," and paste your
  schedule as a spreadsheet (CSV).
- **Add your classes directly:** Create each class on your Classes page (chapter 12), then schedule its
  sessions (chapter 13).

A schedule added this way doesn't sync with anything, so make any changes directly on Student Body,
on your Schedule.

## 12. Your classes [Owner · Manager]

Your Classes page is where you can view and manage all your classes. Each class has its own card showing
whether it's a Draft or Published, and where students can book.

A class is the type of experience you offer, like Barre Sculpt. A session is a specific date and
time when that class takes place. You can find upcoming sessions in your Schedule (chapter 13).

### Publishing your classes

Before you can publish a class, you'll need to add:

- **Class details:** A name, class type, duration, and short description.
- **Booking information:** A booking link and price, as listed on your own website.
- **Location and capacity:** A default location and the number of available spots.

Most of this information will already be filled in for classes imported from your booking system.
To publish your classes:

- **One class:** Open the class from your Classes page and select "Publish" in the panel beside the
  editor. Until the class is ready, the panel lists what's still missing under "To publish," and each
  line's "Add" link takes you to that field.
- **Multiple classes:** Select the classes you want to publish on your Classes page, then select
  "Publish."

You can also publish imported classes from the "[number] imported classes aren't live yet" section:
select "Review and publish," then "Publish" on each class. A class that still books on your own
platform needs a description and a price first.

> **Good to know**
>
> Publishing a class doesn't make it visible to students right away. Your studio must also be live
> on Student Body (chapter 14).

> **Heads up**
>
> Once your studio is live, changes to published classes take effect as soon as you select "Save
> Changes." There's no additional review step.

> **Heads up**
>
> Until you're ready to take bookings on Student Body, leave "Make bookable here" and "Set price" in
> your Classes page turned off. These settings allow students to book directly through Student Body and
> require additional setup (Part 5).

### Creating a class

To add a class, select "New class" on your Classes page. We'll ask for just the essentials, and
you'll add the rest in the editor:

- **Start from:** "A blank class," or "A teacher's program" to use a program one of your instructors
  wrote (see "Teachers' programs" below).
- **Name and Type:** What the class is called, and the type students browse by.
- **Format:** A class, an event, or an appointment (a bookable slot of someone's availability).
- **Duration and Price:** How long the class lasts and what students pay, or "Free."
- **Managed by:** "The studio," or one of your instructors. A class managed by an instructor is theirs:
  it appears on their profile too, and you can edit it but not unpublish or delete it.

Select "Create draft," and the class opens in the editor as a draft.

If you start from a teacher's program, choose the program and we'll ask the instructor. The class
starts as a draft run by your studio, with that instructor as its teacher, and takes the program's
name, words, and photos when they say yes.

### The class editor

To edit a class, open it from your Classes page. The editor has four screens, with a panel beside
them that shows how the class will look and what's still missing:

| Screen | What you can manage |
|---|---|
| **About** | Name, format, type, duration, style, intensity, the languages it's taught in, card color, description, and photos |
| **Booking** | How students book, booking rules, price, cancellation, and a few more options |
| **Place & people** | Where the class happens, how many spots it has, what to bring, equipment, and its teacher |
| **Help students choose** | What the class feels like, who it's for, and what to expect, all optional |

The panel shows a preview of the class card, whether the class is a Draft or Published, and what's
still needed under "To publish." "Publish," "Save draft," and "Save changes" are there too. On a
phone, the panel's summary sits at the top of the screen, and the buttons in a bar at the bottom.

**Class type**\
Your class type determines where your class appears when students browse Student Body. Choose the
option that best describes your class: Yoga, Pilates, Strength, Dance, Meditation, Cycling, Barre,
Movement, or Sound Healing.

> **Heads up**
>
> Classes listed as "Other" won't appear when students browse by class type.

**Language**\
Each class says which languages it's taught in ("Taught in" on the About screen) and which language
its words are written in ("Written in"). Students browsing Student Body in another language can
translate your class information, and a class with nothing under "Taught in" won't appear when
students filter by language.

### Classes that book by WhatsApp

A class can book by WhatsApp. Students choose a session on Student Body, then send the request to
your studio's WhatsApp number, already written. You confirm their place in the chat, and they pay the
studio directly, outside Student Body.

To set it up, open the class's Booking screen and choose "WhatsApp" under "How students book."
Then fill in these fields:

- **Your WhatsApp number:** The number students write to, with its country code, such as
  +351 912 345 678.
- **Your MB WAY number (optional):** A Portuguese mobile number, such as 912 345 678. Students see it
  on the class and pay the studio by MB WAY. Leave it empty if they pay at the class.
- **Price:** What students pay you. It reads "Price (paid by MB WAY)" when you've added an MB WAY
  number, and "Price (paid at the lesson)" when you haven't. Choose "Ticket options" instead of "One
  price" to offer several.

Once a student has booked with you on WhatsApp, record their place on Student Body, so the class
shows the right number of available spots (chapter 13).

### Helping students find the right class

The "Help students choose" screen is optional, but it's one of the best ways to help students
understand what your class is actually like.

Here, you can share details like the difficulty, the overall atmosphere of your class, and what a
session is like. This helps students decide if it's right for them and helps Student Body recommend
it to people who might enjoy it.

The screen holds seven groups. Select one to open it:

- **Feel:** The atmosphere of the room, and how students feel afterward.
- **Challenge and support:** What makes the class challenging and what support is available. Be
  specific about what students can expect.
- **Fit:** Who the class is great for and who it might not be right for.
- **What to expect:** How the session is structured and what students will do.
- **Class flow:** The class in steps, with a photo for each.
- **Attributes:** Group format, drop-in friendly, equipment provided, and rules like "Women only."
- **Music:** Whether music is part of the experience, with a playlist link if you have one.

A group shows "Added" once you've filled something in, and the panel counts how many of the seven
you've completed. Think about how you'd describe your class to someone who's never been before. Be
honest about what to expect, and don't feel like you need to complete every group.

Students filter by intensity, language, atmosphere, and music. "Intensity" is on the About screen,
and every class starts at Moderate until you change it. "Style" says which kind of class it is,
since yin and power flow are both yoga, and a playlist link lets students listen before they book.

**Women only**\
If a class is only for women, open "Attributes" on the "Help students choose" screen and select
"Women only." Students will see a "Women only" label on the class and, beside the booking button,
"This class is for women only. [studio name] sets this rule." They can also find these classes
with the "Women only" filter in Discover.

> **Good to know**
>
> "Women only" is a rule your studio states and enforces. Student Body shows it to students, but
> doesn't check who books.

### Teachers' programs

Some instructors teach the same class at more than one studio, or run it on their own as well. On
Student Body, they can write that class once as a program, with its name, descriptions, and photos,
and use it on each class they teach.

An instructor on your team can offer their program for a class they teach at your studio, and you
can also ask an instructor to use theirs. Either way, nothing changes until the other side accepts.
Offers and suggestions appear at the top of your Classes page, under "Teachers' programs." You can
also start a new class from a program ("Creating a class" above).

Here's what changes when a class uses a program:

- **Words and photos:** The class's name, descriptions, and photos come from the program, and only the
  instructor can change them. On the About screen, the class editor shows the program's card, with
  the instructor's name, in place of those fields.
- **Everything else:** The schedule, prices, bookings, and location stay yours.
- **On your Classes page:** The class shows the instructor's name with "program," for example "Marta's
  program."
- **For students:** When a program runs on more than one public class, each class page shows "A program
  by" and the instructor's name. It links to the program's page, which lists every upcoming session of
  the program, wherever it runs.

To stop using a program, open the class and select "Remove program" on the program's card. The class
will go back to its own text. You'll also need to remove the program before changing the class's default teacher.

Student feedback on a class that uses a program also appears on the program's page. If you hide a
quote, it's hidden from your studio's pages. It can still appear on the instructor's program page if
they've chosen to publish it.

> **Good to know**
>
> If the instructor leaves your team, their program goes with them, and the class goes back to its own
> text. If the class doesn't have a description of its own, your Classes page will show "A class needs a
> description." Write one, or unpublish the class.

## 13. Your schedule [Owner · Manager · Staff]

Your Schedule shows all upcoming sessions at your studio, with options to view them by week or
month. Each session includes the class, instructor, time, and available spots.

If your schedule syncs with a connected booking system (chapter 11), changes to session times,
dates, and cancellations should always be made there.

### Managing individual sessions

You can make a few changes to individual sessions directly on Student Body:

- **Taught by:** Change the instructor for a specific session if they're different from the class's
  usual instructor.
- **Co-teachers:** Add additional instructors teaching alongside the main instructor.
- **View session page:** See what students will see when they view that session.
- **Edit class:** Open the class editor to update the class details (chapter 12).

> **Heads up**
>
> If you manually change an instructor for a session on Student Body, that change will stay in place
> even when your connected schedule syncs. New sessions will use the instructor assigned in your
> booking system.

### Scheduling classes directly on Student Body

You can also schedule classes that aren't in your booking system, such as a one-off
workshop or special event.

- **One-time sessions:** Open the class on your Classes page and select "Schedule Class" to choose a date
  and time.
- **Recurring classes:** Go to Schedule and select "Propose recurring class." Choose the class, day
  and time, location, instructor (or instructors), capacity, and dates.

Recurring classes automatically have sessions scheduled for the next eight weeks.

> **Good to know**
>
> To change or cancel a recurring class you've created on Student Body, contact our team. We'll help
> you make the changes.

### Recording WhatsApp bookings

A booking request sent on WhatsApp reaches your studio's number, not Student Body. Record each place
once you've confirmed it, so the class fills on Student Body as it fills in the chat.

1. In Schedule, select the session, then select "Record WhatsApp bookings." The session page opens,
   with a card marked "Only the studio's team sees this."
2. Under "Add someone who booked on WhatsApp," enter the student's name. You can also add their email
   and WhatsApp number, and the number of places if they've booked more than one.
3. Select "Add to the list."

Each student takes a place, and the card counts them, such as "4 of 6 places taken." When every
place is taken, students see "This class is now full," with a link to "Ask on WhatsApp if a place
opens."

Here's what else you can do on the card:

- **Send the confirmation:** After you add someone, select "Send on WhatsApp" or "Copy." Its link adds
  the place to the student's Student Body account, with a reminder and a calendar entry.
- **Cancel:** Takes a student off the list, and their place opens again.
- **Mark paid:** When a student has paid, select "Paid by MB WAY" or "Paid at the lesson." On a class
  without an MB WAY number, select "Mark paid." "Undo" takes it back.

> **Good to know**
>
> Only the owner and managers can record WhatsApp bookings. Front desk staff with the Staff role
> won't see "Record WhatsApp bookings." The link appears on your studio's own classes once they're
> published.

### Instructor requests

If you've given instructors permission to schedule classes at your locations, they'll be able to
send requests to use those spaces.

You'll find these requests on your Home page under "Location requests," where you can choose to:

- **Approve:** Accept the instructor's request.
- **Always allow:** Let the instructor schedule classes at your location without requesting approval
  each time.
- **Decline:** Reject the request.

# Part 3 — Going live

How to get your studio approved, what students can see before you're live, and how to share your
studio once it's ready.

## 14. Getting approved [Owner · Manager]

### Getting ready to go live

On your Home page, you'll find a "Launch readiness" checklist with seven steps to complete before
your studio can go live.

The checklist updates automatically as you complete each step:

1. **Add a studio bio:** Write a short introduction to your studio.
2. **Add a studio photo:** Upload your logo or a photo of your space.
3. **Add a location:** Add at least one location where your classes take place.
4. **Publish your first class:** Make sure at least one class is ready for students to discover.
5. **Schedule a session:** Add at least one upcoming session.
6. **Invite an instructor:** Add at least one instructor to your team.
7. **Set your profile to public:** Request to make your studio visible to students.

Each step has a "Take me there" link that takes you directly to where you can complete it.

### Asking to go live

Once you've completed the first six steps, you're ready to request approval. You can do this in two
ways:

- **From Home:** Select "Make studio public."
- **From Settings:** Go to `Settings → Studio profile`, find "Visibility," select "Public," and press
  "Save changes."

Once you've requested approval, your studio's status will change from "Draft" to "Under review."
You'll see this at the top of your dashboard and on your Home page.

### While we review

Our team will review your studio profile and schedule, usually within a day. While your studio is
under review:

- **Your studio page:** Anyone with a direct link can view your studio profile.
- **Your classes:** Class pages aren't available yet, and students can't book through Student Body.
- **Discover and search:** Your studio won't appear in search results or Discover until it's
  approved.

Once approved, you'll receive an email and notification letting you know your studio is live. Your
published classes and studio profile will then appear in Discover and search.

> **Good to know**
>
> After your studio's first approval, you can switch between "Public" and "Draft" at any time without
> needing another review.

## 15. Sharing your studio [Owner · Manager]

Your studio has its own page on Student Body at studentbody.pt/[handle], making it easy to share your
classes, schedule, and studio information. You'll find more ways to share your studio under "Share"
in your dashboard.

| Feature | What it does | Where to use it |
|---|---|---|
| **Your link** | Copy a link to your studio page | Instagram bio, WhatsApp groups |
| **Your week, as a story** | An image of your next seven days of classes, made from your schedule as it is now, ready for your Instagram story | Instagram stories |
| **For the front desk** | Create a QR code to print. If you have multiple locations, you can choose which one it opens | Front desk |
| **On your website** | Add your live Student Body schedule directly to your studio's website | Your website |
| **Calendar feed** | Let students subscribe to your published schedule in their calendar app | Front desk, regular students |
| **Links to each class** | Copy a direct link to any of your class pages | Instagram, newsletters, messages |

If your studio uses Squarespace, add a Code block where you'd like your schedule to appear, then
paste in the code from Student Body.

Your schedule will stay up to date automatically.

> **Good to know**
>
> While your studio is under review, only people with a direct link can view your studio page. Your
> class pages won't be available until your studio is approved. See chapter 14 for more details.

# Part 4 — Running your studio

How to keep your schedule and class information up to date, manage student feedback, and see how
your studio is doing on Student Body.

## 16. Keeping everything up to date [Owner · Manager · Staff]

If your schedule syncs from Acuity, bsport, or YOGO, most updates happen automatically every hour
(chapter 11). If you schedule classes directly on Student Body, make your changes on your Schedule
(chapter 13).
We recommend checking your studio page about once a month to make sure your photos, instructor
profiles, and studio information are still up to date.

If your schedule syncs from a connected booking system, a few things to keep in mind:

- **Update your schedule in your booking system**\
  Make changes to session dates, times, and cancellations there. They'll automatically update on
  Student Body within the hour.
- **New class types**\
  New class types added there will appear as drafts on your Classes page. Review the details and publish
  them when they're ready.
- **New instructors**\
  Classes taught by new instructors won't import automatically. Go to `Settings → Connected apps`
  and select "Sync & review" to bring them in.
- **Editing class details**\
  You can update class names and descriptions directly on Student Body without worrying about the
  hourly sync overwriting your changes. A content refresh ("Refresh from Acuity" or "Refresh
  descriptions & images") keeps them too: it only changes the names, descriptions, and images of
  classes you haven't edited here.

## 17. Your students and their feedback [Owner · Manager]

### Your audience

Students can follow your studio on Student Body to stay connected and receive updates from your
studio.

You'll find your followers under `Insights → Audience`.

Students can choose how their names appear to studios, either their full name or their first name
and last initial. You'll only see their email address or phone number if they've chosen to share
that information.

### Communicating with students

There are two ways to communicate with students through Student Body:

- **Message audience:** Send announcements to all your followers or a selected group. These are
  one-way messages, so students can't reply. Groups must have at least five people, and you can send
  up to 10 announcements per day.
- **Student questions:** Students can select "Ask a question" on your studio page to contact you.
  You'll receive a notification when a question comes in.

### Feedback

After attending a class, students who booked through Student Body can share feedback about their
experience.

You'll find this under `Insights → Feedback`, where you can see what students appreciate about your
studio, what could be improved, and any comments they've shared.

Some positive feedback may also appear as quotes on your public studio page. You can choose to hide
these under "Student quotes on your public pages."

> **Good to know**
>
> Students who book through your existing booking system can also leave feedback. When a student
> returns to Student Body after visiting your booking page, we'll ask if they completed their
> booking. If they confirm, they'll be able to share feedback after class. Because this relies on
> students confirming their bookings, you may receive less feedback than studios that take bookings
> directly through Student Body.

## 18. Your numbers [Owner · Manager]

`Insights → Overview` gives you a picture of how your studio is doing over the last 12 weeks,
including bookings, attendance, class capacity, followers, and returning students.

For a closer look, `Insights → Reports` lets you export your data as a spreadsheet (CSV) for 30, 90,
or 365 days, or download a printable report.

`Team → Activity` keeps a record of changes made in your studio's console, so you can see who changed
what.

If your classes book through your existing booking system, Student Body can show you how students
are discovering your classes and finding their way to your booking page.

- **Home:** "Sent to your booking page" shows how many times students clicked "Book on
  [studio name]" this week, compared with the previous week.
- **`Insights → Overview → Reach`**\
  See how students move from discovering your studio to opening your booking page.
  - **Views:** Visits to your pages from students who have accepted analytics cookies. Actual visits
    may be higher.
  - **Link opens:** The number of times students opened your booking page from Student Body.
  - **"Said they booked" and "Confirmed bookings":** What students report after returning from your
    booking page.
  - **"From your website":** Clicks on the Book button in the schedule embedded on your website,
    tracked separately.
- **Fill rate and seats filled:** Shown on Home and in Insights, using your booking system's booking and
  capacity data from the most recent sync.

Bookings, attendance and revenue in Insights count only bookings made directly through Student Body.
Bookings taken through your existing booking system stay in that system.
You can still see your class fill rates and how students discover your studio and interact with your
booking links.

## 19. What your students see [All]

Worth sharing with your front desk team, so they know what students see and how the booking process
works.

- **Finding you**\
  Students can discover your studio through Discover, search, the map, or a link you've shared.
  They can browse on app.studentbody.pt, on their phone or computer.
- **Your studio page**\
  Students can explore your story, photos, instructors, locations, schedule, and follow your studio
  for updates.
- **A class page**\
  Students can see what a class feels like, who it's for, who's teaching, where it takes place, and
  when it's happening. They can also translate the page into their preferred language.
- **Booking**\
  When a student selects "Book on [studio name]," they're taken directly to that class in
  your booking system to complete their booking. The booking happens in your booking system, not Student
  Body.
- **Signing in first**\
  Students who aren't signed in will be asked to sign in or create a free account before booking.
  Students booking through the schedule embedded on your website go directly to your booking system.
- **"Did you get a spot?"**\
  When students return to Student Body, we ask whether they completed their booking. Their response
  helps us understand how often Student Body leads to bookings.
- **Booking on WhatsApp**\
  When a class books by WhatsApp, students select "Book on WhatsApp." WhatsApp opens with their
  request already written, greeting your studio by name, with the class, the day and time, the
  location, and the price. If the class shows your MB WAY number, they're told they "pay the studio
  directly, outside Student Body."

## 20. What your instructors see [Instructor]

- **Their profile:** Every instructor on your roster has a Student Body profile that appears on your
  studio page and on the classes they teach.
- **Claiming a profile:** Instructors you've added as placeholders can claim their profiles using the
  "Claim link" you send them (chapter 10). Once claimed, they can add their own photo and bio, and
  their classes come with them.
- **Teaching elsewhere:** Instructors who work at other studios or run their own classes can bring
  everything together on one profile. Classes at your studio remain managed by your studio.
- **Dashboard access:** Instructors with the Member role can't access your studio dashboard. If they
  need access, you can give them a Manager or Staff role (chapter 10).

# Part 5 — When you're ready: taking bookings on Student Body

Nothing in this section is required to get started.

When you're ready, you can choose to take bookings directly on Student Body, one class at a time.
Students can book in just a few taps, and you'll have access to additional tools like class packs
and discount codes.

This section walks you through how it works.

## 21. Your Stripe account [Owner]

Students who book classes directly on Student Body pay through Stripe, into your own Stripe account.
Your studio is the seller, and Student Body never holds your money.

Stripe charges its standard processing fees and sends payouts to your bank account according to the
schedule you choose.

To get started, open `Settings → Payments`, find the "Payment account" section, and select "Set
up payments." Stripe will guide you through signing in or creating an account, then adding your
business and bank details.

> **Heads up**
>
> The email address you use to start Stripe setup becomes the login for your payment account. If
> your studio already has a Stripe account, use the email associated with that account.

Once setup is complete, the section shows "Connected to Stripe." Select "Manage on Stripe" to view
your payouts, statements, receipts, and disputes.

| What the section shows | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Connected to Stripe" | Your Stripe account is connected and ready to accept payments |
| "Payments are paused" with "Fix it on Stripe" | Stripe needs something from you before payments can resume. Select "Fix it on Stripe" to resolve the issue |
| "Start over with a different email" | Restart setup with another email. Available only before setup is complete or anyone has booked |
| "Switch to a different Stripe account" | Future payments go to the new account. Previous payments remain in the original account |

**How students pay:** Students can pay by card, with a card saved to their Student Body account, or
with Apple Pay or Google Pay on the web. MB WAY is also available if you've enabled it in your Stripe
account.

## 22. Taking bookings on Student Body [Owner · Manager]

1. **Connect Stripe:** Make sure your payment account shows "Connected to Stripe" (chapter 21).
   You'll need this before you can accept paid bookings.
2. **Choose a class:** On your Classes page, open "Review and publish" and select "Make bookable here"
   for the class you want to offer.
3. **Set your price:** Choose how much students will pay to book the class.
4. **Choose your seats:** Set "Seats sold on Student Body" to the number of places you want to make
   available for booking here.

> **Heads up**
>
> If you're also taking bookings through your booking system, make sure the same seats aren't available
> on both platforms. Otherwise, you risk double-booking.
>
> If you use Acuity, you can also send bookings made through Student Body to Acuity by turning on
> "Mirror Student Body bookings into Acuity" under `Settings → Connected apps`.

**Prices.** Classes can be free, have a fixed price, or accept donations. Fixed-price classes can have
one price or multiple ticket options, such as early bird and standard, each with its own price and
optional seat limit.

> **Heads up**
>
> The "Set price" bulk action on your Classes page also changes how selected classes accept bookings. If you're
> only updating prices, edit classes individually to avoid switching them to Student Body bookings
> unintentionally.

## 23. Packs, memberships, and discount codes [Owner · Manager]

### Class packs

Open `Settings → Packs` to create a class pack. Students purchase a set number of credits upfront and
use one credit each time they book an eligible class.

- **Pack details:** Add a name, number of credits, price (EUR), and validity period. Leave the
  validity field empty if the pack doesn't expire. We recommend 90 days, though longer periods may
  work better for some packs.
- **Eligible classes:** Packs work with fixed-price classes that accept bookings on Student Body. To
  exclude a class, turn off "Class packs" in its editor.
- **Ticket options:** Classes with multiple ticket options can't be booked using pack credits.
- **Archiving packs:** Select "Archive" to stop selling a pack. Editing or archiving a pack won't
  affect credits students have already purchased.

Students can purchase class packs directly from your studio page.

### Memberships

A membership is a monthly plan. Members pay by card every month, on the day they joined, and use it to
book classes. Open `Settings → Packs` and select "New membership":

- **Classes:** "Unlimited," or a number under "Classes a month."
- **Weekly cap:** Optional. The most classes a member can book from Monday to Sunday. A late cancel or
  no-show counts.
- **Price a month:** In euros.

A few things to keep in mind:

- **Stripe first:** Students can join a membership only once your Stripe account is set up (chapter 21).
- **Eligible classes:** A membership covers all your classes that accept bookings on Student Body, or
  just the one class you choose. To exclude a class, turn off "Class packs" in its editor, as for packs.
- **Each month:** Classes a member doesn't use end with the month. Members can cancel at any time, and
  the cancellation takes effect at the end of the month.
- **Changing a membership:** Once someone joins, the price, classes, and cap are locked. To change
  them, make a new membership and archive this one. Current members keep their terms.
- **Fees:** Stripe charges your account about 0.7% on recurring payments, on top of card fees.

Students join from your studio page or a class page: they select "Join," then "Join and pay."

### Discount codes

Open `Settings → Discounts` to create discount codes for your classes.

- **Code:** Choose the code students will enter when booking.
- **Discount:** Select a percentage or fixed amount (EUR).
- **Applies to:** Choose whether the code works for every class or a specific class.
- **Usage limits:** Set the total number of uses and how many days the code remains valid.
- **Per-student limit:** Each student can use a code once.
- **Complimentary bookings:** A 100% off discount code can be used to offer a free place in a class.
- **Editing codes:** Once created, a code's terms can't be changed. Create a new code instead. Codes
  that have already been used can be switched off, but not deleted.

## 24. Bookings, check-in, cancellations and refunds [Owner · Manager · Staff]

### Bookings

Open Bookings to see everyone who has booked a class through Student Body, including their ticket,
booking date, and any discounts applied.

Filter bookings by "Upcoming" or "Past," or by active and cancelled bookings.

### Check-in

Open a session in Schedule and select "View class list & check in," or select "Run check-in" from
Home. You can check students in three ways:

- **Individual check-in:** Tap a student's name to mark them present, or select "Mark all present"
  to check in everyone at once.
- **Walk-ins:** Select "Add walk-in" for someone who arrives without a booking.
- **QR code check-in:** Select "Show QR code" and let students scan it with their phone cameras to
  check themselves in.

Students who haven't been marked present are automatically counted as no-shows 24 hours after their
class.

> **Good to know**
>
> Students can leave a private injury note before class. Only the instructor leading that session
> can see it, and it's automatically deleted after class.

### Cancellations

- **When a student cancels:** If they cancel within the free-cancellation window, they'll receive a
  full refund or have their pack credit returned. After that window, they won't receive a refund or
  credit. The window is set for each class, or uses your studio's default under
  `Settings → Studio profile` (24 hours by default).
- **When you cancel a session:** Select "Cancel session" in Schedule. Everyone booked into that
  session receives a full refund or has their pack credit returned, regardless of the cancellation
  window.

### Refunds

Go to `Settings → Payments` to see recent payments and issue refunds.

- **Full refunds:** Select "Refund" to return the full amount and release the student's place in
  class.
- **Email notifications:** Select "Don't email the student" if you'd prefer to contact them yourself.
- **Partial refunds:** Process these directly in Stripe. Student Body records the partial refund, and
  the student keeps their place in class.

> **Heads up**
>
> If one student cancels more than five paid bookings on the same day, refunds for the later
> cancellations appear as "Refund held for review," and you'll get an email for each one. Select
> "Refund" to send it now. Otherwise, it goes back to the student automatically 3 days after the
> cancellation.

Disputes and chargebacks are handled in your Stripe account.

### Booking notifications

To receive an email whenever someone books or cancels a class on Student Body, go to
`Settings → Studio profile`, turn on "Booking activity to your inbox," and enter the email address
where you'd like to receive notifications.

## 25. Invoices and taxes [Owner]

When a student books a class through Student Body, the payment goes to your studio. You're
responsible for issuing invoices or faturas, just as you would for bookings made directly through
your studio.

Student Body sends students a booking confirmation showing what they paid and who they paid, but this
isn't a tax invoice.

Continue issuing faturas through your usual certified invoicing software.

To help reconcile your payments, you can use:

- **`Settings → Payments`:** View individual payments and refunds.
- **Stripe:** Access payment reports, fees, and payouts.
- **Reports:** Export your booking and payment data as spreadsheets.

Your accountant can help you determine how these sales should be recorded.

# Part 6 — Your data and help

Your information, your students, and the support available whenever you need it.

## 26. Your data [Owner]

**What you see about students:** Students choose how their names appear to studios, either in full
or as a first name and initial. You'll only see their email address or phone number if they've
agreed to share their contact details with studios, or if you've entered those details yourself.

**Exporting your data:** Go to `Insights → Reports → All your studio's data` to download a copy of the
information Student Body holds for your studio, including:

- Your studio profile, locations, team, classes, and sessions.
- Bookings, attendance, and waitlists.
- Class packs, discount codes, messages, feedback, connections, and settings.

Only the studio owner can download the full export.

**When we access your dashboard:** If someone from Student Body opens your dashboard to help with a
support request, you'll see it recorded under `Team → Activity` as "opened your dashboard as Student
Body support."

**Closing your studio:** Go to `Settings → Studio profile → Close the studio` to see what will be
removed and what will remain. You'll need to enter your studio's handle to confirm.

> **Heads up**
>
> Closing your studio is permanent. Your locations, team, schedule, class packs, and discount codes
> will be deleted. Your studio's handle will become available again, and any student details you've
> entered manually will be removed.
>
> You can't close your studio while you have upcoming bookings. Be sure to download your data before
> closing.

## 27. Getting help [All]

There are a few ways to reach us if you need a hand:

- **Email:** Write to support@studentbody.pt. We aim to respond within two working days.
- **In the app:** Go to your Account page and select "Contact support."
- **Service status:** Visit status.studentbody.pt to check whether Student Body is experiencing any
  issues. You can also subscribe to email updates.

When contacting support, let us know which studio and page you're working on, what you expected to
happen, and what happened instead. A screenshot is always helpful.

## B. Roles and permissions

| | Owner | Manager | Staff | Member (instructor) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home, Schedule, session changes, check-in | ● | ● | ● | — |
| Bookings | ● | ● | — | — |
| Record WhatsApp bookings and mark them paid | ● | ● | — | — |
| Classes: create and edit | ● | ● | — | — |
| Insights: Overview, Audience, Reports, Feedback | ● | ● | — | — |
| Change one session's time, location or notes | ● | — | — | — |
| Locations, Share | ● | ● | — | — |
| Team: Team members, roles, invitations; Activity | ● | ● | — | — |
| Settings: Studio profile, Connected apps, Packs, Discounts | ● | ● | — | — |
| Settings: Payments, Plan & billing | ● | — | — | — |
| Studio agreement, data exports, closing the studio | ● | — | — | — |

A Member is an instructor on your studio's roster without access to your studio dashboard. Owners,
Managers, and Staff can access the dashboard according to their assigned permissions.

Someone who doesn't teach can have a dashboard role without an instructor profile: invite them with
"Add someone who doesn't teach" (chapter 10).

## C. Glossary

| Word | Means |
|---|---|
| **Class** | An activity you offer, with its own name, description, class type, duration, and booking details |
| **Session** | A specific date and time when a class takes place |
| **Recurring class** | A class that repeats on a regular schedule, such as every Tuesday at 19:00 |
| **Program** | An instructor's class, written once and used on each class they teach, including at your studio when you both agree. Only the instructor edits its words and photos |
| **Draft / Published** | A draft class is only visible in your dashboard. A published class becomes visible to students once your studio is live |
| **Draft / Under review / Live** | Your studio's visibility status. Draft means you're still setting up. Under review means you've requested to go live and we're reviewing your studio. Live means students can discover you on Student Body |
| **Books on [booking system]** | Students discover your class on Student Body but complete their booking through your booking system |
| **Books on WhatsApp** | Students discover your class on Student Body and send their booking request to your studio's WhatsApp number. They pay you directly |
| **Books on Student Body** | Students book and pay directly on Student Body, with payments going into your Stripe account |
| **Placeholder instructor** | An instructor you've added to your roster who hasn't claimed their profile yet |
| **Claim** | Taking ownership of a studio or instructor profile that's already been created for you |
| **Roster** | The instructors associated with your studio |
| **Follower** | A student who follows your studio on Student Body and receives your announcements |
| **Merchant of record** | The business responsible for selling a class and receiving payment. For classes booked on Student Body, that's your studio |
| **Pack / Credit** | A pack is a set of class credits purchased in advance. Each eligible class booking uses one credit |
| **Sync** | The automatic process that keeps your Student Body schedule updated with changes made in your booking system. This happens every hour |

## D. When something looks wrong

| You see | Why it's happening | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **A cancelled session reappears** | It was cancelled on Student Body, but the hourly sync brought it back from your booking system | Cancel the session in your booking system |
| **A new instructor's classes are missing** | The hourly sync doesn't automatically import classes for new instructors | Go to `Settings → Connected apps → Sync & review` |
| **A new class appears as a draft** | New classes imported from your booking system arrive as drafts | Review the class on your Classes page and publish it |
| **Your studio is still Under review** | We haven't finished reviewing your studio yet | You'll usually hear from us within a day. If it's taking longer, get in touch |
| **Your class doesn't appear when students browse by type** | The class type is set to "Other" | Open the class editor and select the most appropriate class type |
| **Your location appears incorrectly on the map** | The address wasn't selected from the suggested address list | Edit your location and select the correct address from the list |
| **Someone at the front desk can't access Bookings** | Their Staff role doesn't include access to Bookings | Assign them the Manager role if they need booking access |
| **An instructor can't access your studio dashboard** | They're listed as a Member and haven't been assigned a dashboard role | Go to `Team → Team members` and assign the appropriate role |
| **Students see "Not bookable here yet"** | The class is set to accept bookings on Student Body, but your Stripe account isn't ready to accept payments | Go to `Settings → Payments → Payment account` and complete your setup or resolve any outstanding issues |
| **Your class description was replaced by Acuity's version** | "Refresh from Acuity" was used on a class you hadn't edited on Student Body | Write the description on Student Body: a class you've edited there keeps your text on the next refresh |
| **Your class description was replaced by bsport's version** | "Refresh descriptions & images" was used on a class you hadn't edited on Student Body | Write the description on Student Body: a class you've edited there keeps your text on the next refresh |

## E. Not offered today

Student Body is continuing to grow, and there are a few features we don't support just yet. If
something on this list would be useful for your studio, we'd love to hear about it. Email us at
support@studentbody.pt. Your feedback helps us decide what to build next.

- Introductory offers and gift cards.
- Invoices or faturas issued directly by Student Body.
- Booking a specific spot within a studio, such as a numbered reformer or mat.
- A studio-facing waitlist view. Students can join a waitlist and be booked automatically when a spot
  becomes available.
- Partial refunds directly through Student Body. These can be processed in Stripe.
- Notes and tags on individual student profiles.
- Integrations with booking systems other than bsport, YOGO, and Acuity.

# Student Body at your studio, for the front desk

A quick guide for the people welcoming students and keeping things running.

## What Student Body is

Student Body helps people discover movement classes, studios, and instructors.
Your studio has its own page, where students can explore your classes, meet your instructors, view
your schedule, and follow the studio for updates.

## Where bookings happen

Classes that book through your studio's existing booking system are still booked there, just as
before. Students who discover one of those classes on Student Body are directed to your studio's
booking page to reserve their place.

For those classes, nothing changes about how you manage bookings at the front desk.

## If you have dashboard access

- **Signing in:** Go to app.studentbody.pt and sign in with your email, Google, or Apple. If you use
  email, we'll send you a sign-in link. Open the menu under your profile picture and select "Studio
  Dashboard."
- **What you can access:** Staff can view Home and Schedule. Managers can also access Bookings,
  Classes, and Insights.
- **Updating the schedule:** If your schedule syncs from your studio's booking system, make changes
  to class times and cancellations there first. Student Body automatically syncs those changes
  within an hour.

## When a student asks

| They ask | You say |
|---|---|
| **"Can I book this on Student Body?"** | "You can find our classes there! When you select Book on [studio name], you'll be taken to our usual booking page." |
| **"Is it cheaper there?"** | "No, our prices are the same. You'll book directly with us, just as you normally would." |
| **"How do I follow the studio?"** | "Find [studio name] on Student Body and tap Follow. You'll get updates from us there." |
| **"The time on Student Body is different"** | "Let me check our schedule in [booking system]. Student Body updates automatically, but sometimes it takes up to an hour." |

## Who to contact

For questions about your studio's classes, bookings, or schedule, speak with the studio owner.

For help with Student Body, contact support@studentbody.pt.

# Student Body at your studio, for instructors

A quick guide to your instructor profile, your classes, and what students can see.

## Your instructor profile

Student Body helps people discover movement classes, studios, and instructors.

As an instructor at your studio, you have your own profile on Student Body. Students can discover
you through your studio's page and the classes you teach.

Your profile can include your photo, a short bio, and all the classes you teach.

## Making the profile yours

If your studio added you before you created an account, a profile has already been set up for you.
You can claim it using the invitation link sent by the studio owner.

- **Sign in:** Use the email address where you received your invitation. You can sign in with an
  email link, Google, or Apple.
- **Claim your profile:** Follow the invitation link to connect the existing profile to your account.
- **Make it yours:** Add your photo, write a short bio, and introduce yourself to students.

Your classes at your studio will already be connected to your profile, so there's no need to add
them again. You don't have to claim your profile for your name to appear on your studio's
classes, but claiming it lets you manage how you present yourself.

## If you teach elsewhere too

Your Student Body profile belongs to you, not to any one studio. You can use the same profile to show
classes you teach at your studio, other studios on Student Body, or independently. Classes hosted
by your studio remain part of your studio's schedule, even when they appear on your
instructor profile.

## What students see

Students can discover your classes on Student Body, learn about your teaching style, see who each
class is suited for, and explore upcoming sessions.
If your studio's classes book through its existing booking system, students who select "Book on
[studio name]" are directed to that booking page.

## Access to your studio's dashboard

Your instructor profile is separate from your studio's dashboard.
If you haven't been assigned a Staff or Manager role, you won't have access to the studio's
management tools. If you need access to help manage classes or schedules, speak with the studio owner.

For questions about your classes at your studio, contact the studio owner.

For help with your Student Body profile, reach us at support@studentbody.pt.
